name: Boeing 737 MAX
summary: Fourth-generation re-engined 737 with CFM LEAP-1B engines; flown in the US by Southwest, United, American and Alaska.

wings: 'AT' split winglet: an upper blade and a sizeable lower blade forming a straight-edged V at the tip, with no curved blending
engines: Larger, rounder LEAP-1B nacelles mounted further forward and higher
Sawtooth chevrons on the rear edge of each nacelle
fuselage: Pointed 737 nose with V-notched cockpit side windows
Slightly taller nose gear gives a nose-up stance on the ground
tail: Reshaped, longer and more pointed tailcone without the stubby wedge
Dorsal fillet sweeping into a tall fin

tellTales: Sawtooth serrations at the back of the engine nacelles
Wingtip split into upper and lower straight blades
Pointed nose on a low-slung single-aisle twin

confusedWith.howToTell: The MAX has sawtooth chevron exhausts, rounder bigger engines, a twin-blade 'AT' winglet and a pointed tailcone; the NG has smooth exhausts and flat-bottomed intakes.
The MAX has a pointed nose, chevron exhausts and a split twin-blade wingtip; the A320neo has a blunt rounded nose, smooth exhausts and curved sharklets.
The P-8 has raked wingtips, smooth NG-style nacelles, few windows and grey Navy paint; the MAX has split winglets and chevron exhausts.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (Southwest, United, American, Alaska; planespotters.net)
